claims.explanation: SC-9 is a protein kinase C (PKC) activator, and its selective killing likely depends on PKC signaling being intact and coupled to growth-inhibitory or differentiation pathways. Tumors with loss of PTEN or activating RAS/BRAF mutations, which can hyperactivate PKC via PI3K/PLCγ signaling, may be more sensitive, while those with mutations in chromatin remodelers or other survival pathways may be protected.

features.basis: PTEN loss enhances PI3K/PKC signaling, observed in multiple sensitive lines
RAS activation can potentiate PKC pathways, seen in sensitive lines
BRAF mutations activate MAPK and may crosstalk with PKC, observed in sensitive melanomas
TP53 mutations are common in sensitive lines, possibly due to impaired DNA damage response
NF1 loss activates RAS, seen in sensitive lines
ARID1A mutations appear in resistant lines, may alter chromatin and survival
PIK3CA mutations in resistant lines may activate AKT independently of PKC
KMT2D mutations in resistant lines suggest epigenetic protection
ATM mutations in resistant lines may reduce sensitivity to stress
EGFR mutations in resistant lung lines may drive alternative survival
SC-9 targets PRKCA; high expression may enhance drug effect
